issues.quote: Mine was exact. I regulated it myself.
issues.fact: L1 says only that her watch was exact at nine. It says nothing about who regulated it.
issues.misreading: The added claim that she regulated her own watch could suggest she had reason or opportunity to adjust it, which might bear on how far her watch can be trusted for the night's readings.

issues.quote: He worked on it for four years. A minute repeater speaks the time when you press the slide. The low notes are the hours. Each quarter is a doubled note. Then come the high notes, one for each minute past the quarter.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the repeater work and no account of how a minute repeater sounds the time.
issues.misreading: The detailed account of how the repeater strikes the hours, quarters and minutes is a whole method for reading the time by sound. A solver could take it as a clue that the striking matters to the timeline, which the sheet never supports.

issues.quote: He told each owner what was wrong with his.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that the master made everyone show their watches at nine. It does not say he commented on each one.
issues.misreading: The added detail that he gave each owner a verdict on the watch could be read as the master having examined the watches closely, which the sheet does not establish.

issues.quote: Madame plays Chopin. We could tell the pieces.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that the piano began and stopped at the stated kitchen-clock times. It says nothing about which pieces were played or how well the kitchen heard them.
issues.misreading: Saying they could identify the pieces suggests the playing was continuous and clearly audible throughout, which might be taken as confirming the piano ran unbroken between the two readings.
